newsitem.title: FRANCE: French employers agree truckers early retirement.
newsitem.headline: French employers agree truckers early retirement.

text.p: A French union spokesman said on Wednesday that employers have agreed to allow striking truckers to retire early, meeting one of the key demands behind a 10-day strike that has hit the French economy hard.

A spokesman for the Force Ouvriere union said employers had agreed after all-night talks to allow truckers to retire at 55 instead of 60. "The accord constitutes a basis for continuing the negotiations," he said.
Under the agreement, reached in marathon talks that went through their third consecutive night, truckers could retire at 55 after 25 years of service with 75 percent of their salary.
The deal is referred to as an "end of career holiday" rather than early retirement.

In a printed statement, the union made it clear there was insufficient progress on the truckers' two remaining key demands, higher pay and shorter working hours, for optimism about a settlement of the strike at this time.

"At this stage of the negotiations and given the stakes, the employers' proposal to raise salaries by one percent is viewed as a veritable provocation," the FO statement said, encouraging truckers at blockades across the country to step up their protests.
